b.dd4a7118d1:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Epístola ad Romános
<r>Rom 8:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Nihil ergo nunc damnatiónis est iis, qui sunt in Christo Iesu, qui non secúndum carnem ámbulant.
<n>2</n> Lex enim spíritus vitæ in Christo Iesu liberávit me a lege peccáti et mortis.
<n>3</n> Nam quod impossíbile erat legi, in quo infirmabátur per carnem: Deus Fílium suum mittens in similitúdinem carnis peccáti, et de peccáto damnávit peccátum in carne,
<n>4</n> Ut iustificátio legis implerétur in nobis, qui non secúndum carnem ambulámus, sed secúndum spíritum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Beáta Dei Génetrix María, cuius víscera intácta pérmanent:
* Hódie génuit Salvatórem sǽculi.
<r>℣.</r> Beáta, quæ crédidit: quóniam perfécta sunt ómnia, quæ dicta sunt ei a Dómino.
<r>℟.</r> Hódie génuit Salvatórem sǽculi.
b.49f9f0b11a:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans
<r>Rom 8:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> There is now therefore no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus, who walk not according to the flesh.
<n>2</n> For the law of the spirit of life, in Christ Jesus, hath delivered me from the law of sin and of death.
<n>3</n> For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh; God sending his own Son, in the likeness of sinful flesh and of sin, hath condemned sin in the flesh;
<n>4</n> That the justification of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Blessed is God's holy Mother, Mary, maiden undefiled.
* This day hath she brought forth the Saviour of the world.
<r>℣.</r> Blessed is she that believed; for there is a performance of all those things which were told her from the Lord.
<r>℟.</r> This day hath she brought forth the Saviour of the world.
b.ec0ba51989:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ad gáudia paradísi perdúcat nos misericórdia Christi.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Rom 8:5-8</r>
<n>5</n> Qui enim secúndum carnem sunt: quæ carnis sunt, sápiunt. Qui vero secúndum spíritum sunt, quæ sunt spíritus, séntiunt.
<n>6</n> Nam prudéntia carnis, mors est: prudéntia autem spíritus, vita et pax.
<n>7</n> Quóniam sapiéntia carnis inimíca est Deo: legi enim Dei non est subiécta: nec enim potest.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Beáta víscera Maríæ Vírginis, quæ portavérunt ætérni Patris Fílium: et beáta úbera, quæ lactavérunt Christum Dóminum:
* Qui hódie pro salúte mundi de Vírgine nasci dignátus est.
<r>℣.</r> Dies sanctificátus illúxit nobis: veníte, gentes, et adoráte Dóminum.
<r>℟.</r> Qui hódie pro salúte mundi de Vírgine nasci dignátus est.
b.10de70d741:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>Rom 8:5-8</r>
<n>5</n> For they that are according to the flesh, mind the things that are of the flesh; but they that are according to the spirit, mind the things that are of the spirit.
<n>6</n> For the wisdom of the flesh is death; but the wisdom of the spirit is life and peace.
<n>7</n> Because the wisdom of the flesh is an enemy to God; for it is not subject to the law of God, neither can it be.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Blessed be the womb of the Virgin Mary, which bore the Son of the Eternal Father, and blessed be the paps which give suck to Christ our Lord.
* This day hath He been pleased for the salvation of the world to be born of a Virgin.
<r>℣.</r> This day which is breaking is holy; O come, ye Gentiles, and worship the Lord.
<r>℟.</r> This day hath He been pleased for the salvation of the world to be born of a Virgin.
b.592b03c813:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<r>Rom 8:9-11</r>
<n>9</n> Vos autem in carne non estis, sed in spíritu: si tamen Spíritus Dei hábitat in vobis. Si quis autem Spíritum Christi non habet: hic non est eius.
<n>10</n> Si autem Christus in vobis est: corpus quidem mórtuum est propter peccátum, spíritus vero vivit propter iustificatiónem.
<n>11</n> Quod si Spíritus eius, qui suscitávit Iesum a mórtuis, hábitat in vobis: qui suscitávit Iesum Christum a mórtuis, vivificábit, et mortália córpora vestra, propter inhabitántem Spíritum eius in vobis.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Verbum caro factum est, et habitávit in nobis: cuius glóriam vídimus, quasi Unigéniti a Patre,
* Plenum grátiæ et veritátis.
<r>℣.</r> In princípio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum.
<r>℟.</r> Plenum grátiæ et veritátis.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Plenum grátiæ et veritátis.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
<n>(Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem)</n> Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
b.61e996b9be:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<r>Rom 8:9-11</r>
<n>9</n> But you are not in the flesh, but in the spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.
<n>10</n> And if Christ be in you, the body indeed is dead, because of sin; but the spirit liveth, because of justification.
<n>11</n> And if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead, dwell in you; he that raised up Jesus Christ from the dead, shall quicken also your mortal bodies, because of his Spirit that dwelleth in you.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Verbum caro factum est, et habitávit in nobis: cujus glóriam vídimus, quasi Unigéniti a Patre,
* Plenum grátiæ et veritátis.
<r>℣.</r> In princípio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum.
<r>℟.</r> Plenum grátiæ et veritátis.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> Plenum grátiæ et veritátis.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>W</c>e praise thee, O God, * we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.
All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.
To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.
To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.
<n>bow head</n> Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;
Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.
The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.
The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.
The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.
The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;
The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.
Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;
Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.
Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.
Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.
<n>During the following verse all make a profound bow:</n> When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.
When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.
Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.
We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.
<n>Kneel for the following verse</n> We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.
Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.
O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.
Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.
Day by day * we magnify thee;
<n>During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow.</n> And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.
Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.
O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.
O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.
O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

b.f7f2477463:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>C</c>oncéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut nos Unigéniti tui nova per carnem Natívitas líberet; quos sub peccáti iugo vetústa sérvitus tenet.
<h>P</h>er eúndem Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoratio S. Silvestri Papæ et Confessoris</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Euge, serve bone et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, dicit Dóminus.

<r>℣.</r> Iustum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas.
<r>℟.</r> Et osténdit illi regnum Dei.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>a, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut beáti Silvéstri Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis veneránda solémnitas, et devotiónem nobis áugeat et salútem.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.e751a9d920:

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.

b.8bdfdc96fd:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>K</c>aléndis Ianuárii Luna vicésima tértia. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>C</h>ircumcísio Dómini nostri Iesu Christi, et Octáva Nativitátis eiúsdem.
<h>R</h>omæ pássio sanctæ Martínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, sub Alexándro Imperatóre, divérsis tormentórum genéribus cruciáta, tandem, gládio percússa, martýrii palmam adépta est. Ipsíus vero festum tértio Kaléndas Februárii recólitur.
<h>C</h>æsaréæ, in Cappadócia, deposítio sancti Basilíi, cognoménto Magni, Epíscopi, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris; qui, témpore Valéntis Imperatóris, doctrína et sapiéntia insignítus omnibúsque virtútibus exornátus, mirabíliter effúlsit, et Ecclésiam advérsus Ariános et Macedoniános inexpugnábili constántia deféndit. Eius autem festívitas potíssimum ágitur décimo octávo Kaléndas Iúlii, quo die Epíscopus ordinátus est.
<h>A</h>pud montem Senárium, in Etrúria, natális sancti Bonfílii Confessóris, e septem Fundatóribus Ordinis Servórum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis, quam cum idem impénse coluísset, ab ipsa in cælum repénte evocátus est. Illíus porro ac Sociórum festum prídie Idus Februárii celebrátur.
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Almáchii Mártyris, qui, cum díceret: «Hodie Octavæ Domínici diéi sunt, cessáte a superstitiónibus idolórum et a sacrifíciis pollútis,» proptérea, iubénte Præfécto Urbis Alípio, a gladiatóribus occísus est.
<h>I</h>tem Romæ, via Appia, corónæ sanctórum mílitum trigínta Mártyrum, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre.
<h>A</h>pud Spolétum sancti Concórdii, Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui, tempóribus Antoníni Imperatóris, primo cæsus fústibus, dehinc equúleo suspénsus, ac póstea macerátus in cárcere, ibíque Angélica visitatióne confortátus, demum gládio vitam finívit.
<h>E</h>ódem die sancti Magni Mártyris.
<h>I</h>n Africa beáti Fulgéntii, Ruspénsis Ecclésiæ Epíscopi, qui, témpore Wandálicæ persecutiónis, ob cathólicam fidem eximiámque doctrínam, ab Ariánis multa perpéssus et in Sardíniam relegátus est; atque tandem, ad própriam Ecclésiam redíre permíssus, vita et verbo clarus, sancto fine quiévit.
<h>T</h>eáte, in Aprútio citerióre, natális sancti Iustíni, eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, sanctitáte vitæ ac miráculis clari.
<h>I</h>n território Lugdunénsi, monastério Iurénsium, sancti Eugéndi Abbátis, cuius vita virtútibus et miráculis plena refúlsit.
<h>A</h>pud Silviníacum, in Gállia, sancti Odilónis, Abbátis Cluniacénsis, qui primus Commemoratiónem ómnium Fidélium Defunctórum, prima die post festum ómnium Sanctórum, in suis monastériis fíeri præcépit; quem ritum póstea universális Ecclésia recípiens comprobávit.
<h>R</h>omæ natális sancti Vincéntii Maríæ Strambi, Epíscopi Maceraténsis et Tolentíni, Congregatiónis a Cruce et Passióne Iesu sodális, pastoráli zelo præclári, quem Pius Papa Duodécimus inter Sanctos rétulit.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ deposítio sanctæ Euphrósynæ Vírginis, quæ in monastério virtúte abstinéntiæ ac miráculis cláruit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.de8b26f14a:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>anuary 1st 2027, the 23rd day of the Moon,
<h>T</h>he morrow is the Octave of the Birth of our Lord Jesus Christ, upon the which day is commemorated His Circumcision.
<h>U</h>pon the same 1st day of January, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy virgin Martina, who was put to diverse torments, under the Emperor Alexander, and at length gained the crown of martyrdom by the sword, whose feast we keep upon the 30th day of the month of January.
<h>A</h>t Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the burial of the holy Basil, bishop of Caesarea (in the year 379), whose feast we keep upon the 14th day of June. Which is the day whereon he was ordained a bishop.
<h>A</h>t Monte Senario, in Tuscany, the blessed confessor Bonfiglio, one of the seven founders of the order of servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary, to whom he was devoted and by whom he was suddenly called away to heaven (in the year 1262).
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyr Almachius, who was slain by gladiators (about the year 404) at the command of Alpius, prefect of the city, because he said: "This is the Octave of the Lord's Birth, cease from your idolatrous superstitions, and your unclean sacrifices."
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, upon the Appian Way, thirty holy soldiers who were crowned with martyrdom, under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>A</h>t Spoleto, in the time of the Emperor Antonine, the holy martyr, the priest Concordius. He was first cudgelled, then racked, and afterwards suffered imprisonment wherein he was comforted by a visit of angels, and at length was delivered from this life by the sword.
<h>O</h>n the same day, the holy martyr Magnus.
<h>I</h>n Africa, blessed Fulgentius, bishop of the Church of Ruspa (in the year 508), who at the time of the persecution under the Vandals, suffered much at the hands of the Arians because of his Catholic faith, and his eminent teaching. He was exiled to Sardinia (in the year 510); but was at length (in the year 523) allowed to return to his own church, where (in the year 533) he died a holy death, famous for his life and his words.
<h>A</h>t Chieti, in Abruzzo Citeriore, holy Justin, bishop of that city, famous for the holiness of his life, and for the miracles worked through him (in the year 543).
<h>A</h>t the monastery of St. Claude, upon the Jura Mountains, in the country of Lyon, holy (4th) Eugendus, Abbot (of Condat), whose life was illustrious for his graces and miracles (in the year 510).
<h>A</h>t Senlis (in the year 1049), holy Odilo, (6th) Abbot of Cluny (elected in the year 994), who first commanded that in his monasteries a commemoration of all the faithful departed should be made upon the first day after the festival of All Saints, the which custom the Universal Church hath since approved by adopting it.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria (in the year 470), the burial of the holy virgin Euphrosyne, who shone in her nunnery as a great light by the power of her self-denial and her miracles.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
